source.title: TraceRouter: Robust Safety for Large Foundation Models via Path-Level Intervention
source.authors: Chuan-Cheng Shi; Shang-Ze Li; Wen-Jun Lu; Wen-Hua Wu; Cong Wang; Zi-Feng Cheng; Fei Shen; T. Chua

record.tranche_reason: It measures safety under prefill attacks and compares neuron-level with path-level interventions, using behavioral and intervention measures different from the claim’s original fine-tuning or KL measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test harmful or benign fine-tuning, per-token KL, decoding changes, or safety-training objectives. Table 2 reports other jailbreak conditions, but only Prefill and Template+Prefill directly address the named prefill condition. Figure 7's intervention-level comparison is described in text but its numerical values are available only in the figure.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a defense-method paper. Table 2, however, reports original (undefended) LLaMA3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct defense success rates under Prefill, Template+Prefill, Template-only and GCG attacks. Those numbers bear on V4 in new models. The same table also runs DeepAug (Qi et al.'s deep safety alignment) under the same attacks, which bears on V7's robustness. The activation-path experiments (Table 3, Figure 7) do not measure weight or rank localization of safety in safety-trained models.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors argue harmful semantics propagate via distributed cross-layer causal paths, challenging the locality hypothesis. They argue that suppressing those paths at inference time beats neuron-level and state-of-the-art defenses on adversarial robustness with negligible utility loss (e.g., MMLU drop of 0.5-0.8).
record.recipe_differences: Inference-time SAE/FIS-guided activation-path intervention; not fine-tuning aligned models on harmful or benign examples, and no per-token KL measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Prefill and Template+Prefill attack conditions; path-level intervention outperforms the neuron-level comparison; the paper also reports that onset-layer selection and suppression strength affect results, but those are not tests of the listed claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Suppressing SAE-identified cross-layer activation paths raises DSR, and amplifying them lowers it, in SD1.4, FLUX and Show-o2 (nudity). Path-level suppression beats isolated-neuron suppression (Figure 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful-concept generation is mediated by sparse cross-layer activation paths rather than isolated neurons; activation-level, not a weight/rank safety localization.

record.code_released: not stated (the paper says code will be publicly released, but gives no URL)
record.problems: The prefill results report DSR rather than harmful-completion rates and lack a matched no-prefill comparison. The neuron-versus-path comparison gives no numerical values in the text. The causal path experiments manipulate activations and do not establish localization in weights or ranks. No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: Other Table 2 attack conditions (GCG, AutoDAN, and Template without Prefill) were not extracted because the text does not identify them as the compliant-prefill, suffix, or decoding-change conditions named in V4. General-utility scores and image-generation results were omitted because they do not measure the listed claims.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or position analysis.
Decoding changes are not tested. There is no no-attack baseline for either LLM.
No weight or rank localization of safety. The path interventions are activation-level defenses, mostly in diffusion models.
No analysis of the data or objective causes of shallowness.
Only DeepAug under jailbreak attacks is tested. Fine-tuning attacks and per-token analysis of the deepened model are not tested.

missing.what: Original-model Template-only DSR (LLaMA3 98, Mistral 2), the matched comparator for Template+Prefill.
Original-model GCG (suffix) DSR: LLaMA3 88, Mistral 4. AutoDAN: 87 and 22.
DeepAug (Qi et al. deep alignment) DSR under all five attacks for both models. Examples: Prefill 59 and 56; Template+Prefill 3 and 7; AutoDAN 40 on LLaMA3.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. The V4 evidence is a side product of the baseline columns in a defense table, and only LLaMA3 shows a clean prefill effect, because Mistral is unsafe under all attacks. How the prefill is delivered is unclear: Figure 6 shows the 'Sure, here's...' text as the query, so it may not be a true assistant-turn prefill. The DeepAug numbers come from these authors' reimplementation, with no uncertainty reported. Rows r2/r4/r6/r8 are the study's own method and were relinked to none.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning and refusal/compliance changes after fine-tuning.
Benign-data fine-tuning and resulting harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence by response position.
No matched prefill-versus-no-prefill comparison of harmful completion rates; suffixes and decoding changes are not tested.
Does not edit or quantify weights or ranks; the interventions are activation-level neuron/path manipulations, so parameter/rank localization is not established.
Whether safety data or training objectives produce shallow safety.
Safety training designed to spread behavior beyond early response tokens and its robustness.

rows.subject: LLaMA3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated original model under a Prefill jailbreak attack.
rows.measure: Defense success rate (DSR; higher indicates greater safety)
rows.note: The reported DSR indicates vulnerability under Prefill, but the table does not give a matched no-prefill result or a harmful-completion rate.
rows.check: Original LLaMA3 Prefill DSR is 41, so 59% of attempts succeed. There is no no-attack baseline; the nearest comparator is Template-only DSR 98, which is not extracted. The bypass is substantial but incomplete.

rows.subject: LLaMA3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated TraceRouter-enhanced model under a Prefill jailbreak attack.
rows.measure: Defense success rate (DSR; higher indicates greater safety)
rows.note: TraceRouter maintains high safety under Prefill; this is not a matched test of the original model's prefill effect.
rows.check: This is the study's own method compared with others, not a measure of the prefill vulnerability arising in the model. It should not be linked to V4.

rows.subject: LLaMA3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated original model under a combined Template and Prefill jailbreak attack.
rows.measure: Defense success rate (DSR; higher indicates greater safety)
rows.note: Very low DSR indicates vulnerability in this combined attack condition; the paper does not report harmful-completion rates or a matched no-prefill condition.
rows.check: Template+Prefill DSR is 2, against Template-only DSR 98 in the same table, so adding prefill collapses refusal. The Template-only comparator is missing from the rows.

relationships.condition: Original LLaMA3-8B-Instruct, Prefill and Template+Prefill attacks
relationships.reason: Prefill drops DSR to 41 (r1). Template+Prefill gives DSR 2 versus Template-only 98 (r3, Table 2), so a compliant opening defeats refusal.
relationships.display_finding: Prefill alone lowered the defense success rate to 41, and Template+Prefill lowered it to 2 against 98 for the template alone.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Original LLaMA3-8B-Instruct, Prefill and Template+Prefill attacks
source_check.reason: Table 2 reports DSR 41 under Prefill and 2 under Template+Prefill, versus 98 under Template alone, supporting opening bypasses.

relationships.reason: Based on the text (Table 2, no row): GCG gives DSR 88, so suffix attacks mostly fail here, unlike prefill (compare r1).
relationships.display_finding: GCG gives a defense success rate of 88, so suffix attacks mostly fail on this model, unlike prefilling.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Table 2 reports GCG DSR 88: bypass is limited in this condition, substantially weaker than under Prefill.

relationships.condition: DeepAug on LLaMA3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct, Prefill alone
relationships.reason: Based on the text (Table 2, no row): Prefill DSR rises 41 to 59 and 1 to 56. These are partial gains, well below other defenses (95-100).
relationships.display_finding: Defense success rate under prefill attacks rose from 41 to 59 on LLaMA3 and from 1 to 56 on Mistral, well short of the 95–100 that other defenses reached.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: DeepAug on LLaMA3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct, Prefill alone
source_check.reason: Table 2 reports original → DeepAug Prefill DSR of 41 → 59 and 1 → 56, respectively: improvements leave substantial vulnerability.

relationships.condition: DeepAug under Template+Prefill (both models) and AutoDAN (LLaMA3)
relationships.reason: Based on the text (Table 2, no row): Template+Prefill DSR is 3 and 7, barely above the originals' 2 and 4. LLaMA3 AutoDAN DSR falls 87 to 40.
relationships.display_finding: Defense success rate under Template+Prefill was 3 and 7, barely above the original models' 2 and 4, and LLaMA3's AutoDAN defense success rate fell from 87 to 40.

source_check.notes: The pack lists no rows to check; verdicts were checked directly against Table 2. DeepAug training details and attack sample sizes are not supplied, limiting interpretation of small DSR differences.
